title: Scalable Audiovisual Masked Autoencoders for Efficient Affective Video Facial Analysis
abstract: Affective video facial analysis (AVFA) has emerged as a key research field for building emotion-aware intelligent systems, yet this field continues to suffer from limited data availability. In recent years, the self-supervised learning (SSL) technique of masked autoencoders (MAEs) has gained momentum, with growing adaptations in audiovisual contexts. While scaling up has proven essential for breakthroughs in general multimodal learning domains, its specific impact on AVFA remains largely unexplored. Another core challenge in this field is capturing both intra- and intermodal correlations through scalable audiovisual representations. To tackle these issues, we propose AVF-MAE++, a family of audiovisual MAE models designed to efficiently investigate the scaling properties in AVFA while enhancing cross-modal correlation modeling. Our framework introduces a dual masking strategy across audio and visual modalities and strengthens modality encoders with a more holistic design to better support scalable pretraining. Additionally, we present an iterative audiovisual correlation learning module that improves correlation learning within the SSL paradigm, addressing the limitations of previous methods. To support smooth adaptation and reduce overfitting risks, we introduce a progressive semantic injection strategy, organizing the model training into 3 structured stages. Extensive experiments conducted on 17 datasets, covering 3 major AVFA tasks, demonstrate that AVF-MAE++ achieves consistent state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks. Comprehensive ablation studies highlight the importance of each proposed component and provide deeper insights into the design choices driving these improvements. Our code and models have been publicly released at Zenodo.

title: A Graph-Based Method for Molecular Spectral Line Identification
abstract: To address the high computational cost associated with molecular identification in spectral lines, we propose a graph-based feature learning framework to determine the molecular composition of spectral lines that incorporates rule-driven and node-level constraints to enhance identification accuracy. The approach begins with a sliding-window technique to extract localized spectral features that are then represented as nodes within a heterogeneous graph. To maintain semantic consistency across chemically diverse molecular species, rule-based constraints are introduced. Additionally, node-level constraints are employed to prevent the random walk process from becoming trapped in local cycles. The random walk mechanism is further refined through the integration of 2 parameters that guide node selection. Specifically, we design a frequency-aware sampling strategy in which transition probabilities are dynamically updated according to the number of times each node is used, combined with a stochastic modulation factor to enhance exploration and reduce sampling bias. Furthermore, a dynamic rule selection mechanism is employed to adaptively guide the random walk process in response to the evolving topological structure of the graph. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for molecular identification is validated using simulated data, achieving a recall rate of 94.63%. The method is then applied to the real G327 region, where molecular spectral lines are first identified and then used as inputs for XCLASS fitting to further verify the performance of the proposed algorithm. Moreover, the spatial map of molecular counts within spectral cubes is generated, demonstrating the capability for detailed chemical structure analysis.

title: Semi-Implicit Temporal Variational Graph Autoencoder for Dynamic Graph Generation
abstract: Graph simulation has emerged as a practical route to release realistic yet privacy-preserving network data, especially for temporal graphs that evolve through node and edge arrivals. However, prevailing approaches rely on temporal random walks that introduce sampling bias and become prohibitively costly at scale and impose Gaussian variational priors that fail to capture the heavy-tailed dynamics of real systems. We present a semi-implicit temporal variational graph autoencoder (SIT-VGAE) for high-fidelity temporal graph generation. SIT-VGAE samples localized ego-graphs and encodes them with a temporal graph attention network (TGAT) augmented with learnable time embeddings, capturing structural and temporal dependencies without random walk preprocessing. To overcome restrictive priors, we adopt semi-implicit variational inference in which a neural mixer defines an expressive, reparameterizable posterior family that better fits non-Gaussian dynamics. A lightweight decoder maps latent codes to timestamped edge distributions, whose assembled snapshots form generated temporal graphs. The model is trained to maximize a variational lower bound coupling a likelihood over edges with a Kullback–Leibler regularizer. Across multiple real temporal graph datasets, SIT-VGAE achieves superior simulation fidelity on structural statistics, while reducing training and generation time compared with random-walk-based and Gaussian prior baselines. The resulting framework scales to large graphs via TGAT encoding and amortized inference, offering a practical, efficient, and expressive solution for realistic temporal network synthesis.

title: FFD-DHG: Financial Fraud Detection Based on Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning
Probing Privacy Risks in Deep Neural Networks: A Jacobian Rank-Based Analysis of Intermediate Layers
abstract: Deep learning models are known to be vulnerable to privacy attacks that can reconstruct or infer sensitive information from the training data. While many privacy assessment methods exist, they are often computationally prohibitive or overlook the considerable information leakage occurring from the model’s intermediate layers. This paper introduces an efficient, attack-independent framework for quantifying privacy risks by analyzing the sensitivity of these internal representations. We discover that the rank of the Jacobian matrix of an intermediate layer’s output with respect to the model’s input serves as a robust proxy for privacy vulnerability. Specifically, we analyze the dynamics of the Jacobian rank throughout training, proposing 2 metrics, rank recovery (RR) and normalized rank recovery (NRR), to specifically quantify a layer’s dynamic transition from generalization to memorization. Through extensive experiments on a diverse range of computer vision models and datasets, including modern residual networks, we demonstrate a strong and consistent positive correlation between our proposed rank-based metrics and the success rates of membership inference attacks. Our findings reveal that deeper layers, which exhibit considerably higher RR, are the primary sources of privacy leakage. This work provides an actionable methodology for developers to identify high-risk layers in real time, facilitating the development of more secure and privacy-preserving machine learning systems without the need for expensive adversarial simulations.

title: Neural Network-Aided Linear Parameter-Varying Modeling and Finite-Time Control for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Irresponsible driving behavior remains one of the primary causes of road accidents. Given the limited effectiveness of repressive measures, this study proposes an intelligent-vehicle-based solution aimed at enhancing driving safety. The proposed approach focuses on the real-time estimation of unmeasured vehicle states and the torque applied by the driver, which are critical for improving shared control between human and automated systems. To achieve this, a linear parameter-varying model is developed to represent the vehicle’s nonlinear dynamics. The varying parameters of the linear parameter-varying model are estimated using an artificial neural network, ensuring both robustness and adaptability to dynamic driving conditions. Simultaneously, a finite-time sliding mode controller is designed to ensure rapid convergence of tracking error, enhancing system responsiveness. The integrated estimation and control framework is validated through MATLAB and Simulink simulations. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately estimating key states and managing control under a human–machine cooperative driving scenario. This approach contributes to the advancement of intelligent vehicle systems by promoting safer and more reliable interaction between drivers and automated controllers.

title: Identifying Financial Risk Contagion with Large Language Models and Temporal Graph Learning
abstract: Fostering economic growth, particularly the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, is central to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8. Small and medium-sized enterprises can secure bank loans with the help of guarantors, forming interconnected networked-loans. While essential for access to credit, networked-loans can also amplify risk contagion and thus are vulnerable to epidemic financial crises. Previous research has failed to capture nuanced financial semantics and analyze the mechanisms of risk contagion. We designed FinDoctor to tackle these challenges. FinDoctor leverages large language models to extract context-aware features from unstructured financial text. It then combines temporal graph neural networks with the susceptible, exposed, infectious, recovered epidemiological model to identify financial risk contagion. This enables both accurate prediction and targeted risk mitigation. Evaluated on 2 real-world datasets, FinDoctor achieves state-of-the-art performance, with area under the curve scores of 88% and 89%. We further develop an interactive application that visualizes risk propagation and supports targeted intervention. Our work provides a full-cycle solution to identify financial risk contagion in networked-loans.

title: Orthogonality in Quantum-Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Investigation on Multiqubit Encoding
abstract: The “black-box” nature of deep learning models fundamentally limits their reliability in critical applications. Tensor networks (TNs), drawing on their interpretable, quantum-probabilistic foundations, offer a promising pathway toward more transparent machine learning (ML). However, a systematic understanding of their capabilities and limitations remains an open challenge. Here, we establish a fundamental connection between a core property of quantum systems, namely, the catastrophe of orthogonality (COO), and the representational power and generalization performance of quantum-probabilistic TN models. Taking the Fashion Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology dataset, we propose 2 multiqubit data encoding schemes and demonstrate that key hyperparameters, such as the number of qubits, feature count, and mapping angle, modulate the onset of COO. This control mechanism directly dictates the model’s capacity, revealing that over-fitting can be interpreted as a specific regime of the quantum state space. Our work provides a theoretical lens, grounded in quantum many-body physics, for interpreting ML models. It positions TNs not merely as efficient computational tools but as a foundational framework for building inherently interpretable and reliable ML models.

title: Identification of Difficult Laryngoscopy via Double-Pose Feature Clustering Network in Patients with Cervical Spondylosis
abstract: Background: The identification of difficult laryngoscopy is a critical skill for anesthesiologists, particularly in high-risk procedures such as cervical spine surgery, which demands heightened accuracy in preoperative airway assessment. This study developed a deep learning algorithm, the double-pose feature clustering network (DPFCNet), designed to improve the identification of patients with difficult laryngoscopy through comprehensive analysis of neutral and extended cervical spine x-ray images. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 14,407 patients who underwent elective cervical spine surgery under general anesthesia (July 2016 to July 2023) were initially enrolled. Following rigorous screening, 1,568 participants were eligible and included in the analysis, comprising 319 difficult laryngoscopy cases and 1,249 easy laryngoscopy cases. The study evaluated the effectiveness of a deep learning model for identifying difficult laryngoscopy that was developed using a ResNet-based feature extraction module with dual-position image fusion technology and systematically compared it against conventional bedside assessments using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) analysis. Results: Conventional clinical indicators showed poor predictive capacity for difficult laryngoscopy: thyromental distance (AUC = 0.594), neck circumference (AUC = 0.662), inter-incisor gap (AUC = 0.607), and modified Mallampati test (AUC = 0.624). Their combination achieved AUC = 0.743. In contrast, DPFCNet considerably outperformed conventional methods with AUC = 0.866, demonstrating superior discriminative power. Conclusion: This study employed a deep learning model for the comprehensive analysis of both neutral and extended cervical spine x-ray images, considerably improving the prediction accuracy of difficult laryngoscopy. DPFCNet provides an effective decision-support tool for preoperative risk stratification in cervical spondylosis patients.

title: FSFDLLM: Financial Statement Fraud Detection Aided by Large Language Models
abstract: Financial reporting fraud poses a considerable threat to financial market stability. Traditional detection methods predominantly rely on quantitative data analysis while neglecting the informational value of textual disclosures, and existing text analysis approaches suffer from 3 critical limitations: inadequate interpretability, poor domain adaptability, and absence of temporal continuity modeling. This paper proposes the financial statement fraud detection large language model (FSFDLLM) framework, which leverages large language models (LLMs) to achieve in-depth textual feature extraction and interpretable reasoning. Our methodology addresses 3 key challenges: (a) Specifically, we develop a structured prompting mechanism to guide the LLM in conducting the fraud risk assessment of financial texts while generating explanatory rationales. (b) We construct a hybrid learning architecture that integrates LLM-generated pseudo-labels and rationale chains as enhanced features with structured financial data for joint classification model training. (c) The framework has 3 distinctive features: First, it overcomes the domain transfer bottleneck in conventional natural language processing (NLP) models by harnessing the LLM’s semantic comprehension to accurately capture domain-specific financial terminology. Second, it establishes an auditable decision evidence chain through LLM-generated explanatory rationales, thereby enhancing regulatory compliance. Third, it captures continuous fraud patterns by modeling temporal financial indicators and inter-period textual semantic correlations. Experimental evaluations on a real-world listed company dataset demonstrate that our framework considerably outperforms baseline models in key metrics including F1-score and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), while the generated explanatory text provides verifiable semantic evidence for regulatory scrutiny. This study presents a cross-modal solution for financial statement fraud detection (FSFD) that harmonizes high accuracy with interpretability, offering practical value for enhancing financial regulatory technology tools.

title: Traffic-Aware Electric Vehicle Charge-Route Planning Using Data-Driven Ant Colony Optimization
abstract: Charge-route planning (CRP) optimizes the route with charging schedules for electric vehicles (EVs) in order to minimize time and expense, thereby enhancing the overall user experience, especially considering the prolonged charging durations of EVs. Efficiently solving CRP is challenging due to dynamic traffic conditions and complex constraints associated with EV driving and charging. To address this challenge, we propose data-driven traffic-aware ant colony optimization (DDTA-ACO), a framework that tightly integrates predictive and reactive strategies for superior charge-route optimization. First, we propose a high-fidelity, data-driven charge-route time estimation (CRTE) model to accurately predict travel times under dynamic conditions. Then, we design a synergistic search mechanism based on 2 complementary operators: repair-and-proactive avoidance (RPA) and elite adaptive search (EAS). RPA proactively avoids unpromising regions, while EAS intensifies the search in elite regions. Together, they learn from failures and successes to efficiently explore the complex search space. Experiments conducted on 2 real-world datasets demonstrate that DDTA-ACO outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms, showcasing its superior effectiveness for practical, large-scale CRP problems.

title: Large Language Model-Enhanced Mutual Node-Edge Reinforcement for Inductive Fraud Detection in Financial Systems
abstract: Financial fraud detection requires advanced pattern recognition capabilities to address evolving risks. While existing graph neural networks (GNNs) have improved relational modeling, they still face limitations in synthesizing multi-modal features and handling unseen fraud patterns. This paper proposes large language model-enhanced mutual node-edge reinforcement (LLM-EMNER) for inductive fraud detection in financial systems. Our framework first leverages an LLM to separately generate features for nodes and edges, drawing upon their respective descriptions. Then, we develop an edge-aware graph encoder that dynamically fuses node attributes with transaction edge features through (a) a cross-modal attention mechanism that establishes mutual reinforcement between user nodes and transaction edges, (b) adaptive neighbor selection based on temporal-semantic similarity, and (c) edge-projected feature aggregation that preserves structural patterns. The generated node embeddings are then fed into a softmax classifier fine-tuned with contrastive learning objectives, leveraging the superior capability of contrastive learning in identifying complex fraud patterns from heterogeneous features. The LLM-EMNER component specifically employs a dual-stream architecture where edge features guide node representation updates, while node states refine edge semantics, creating dynamic feature reinforcement. For inductive learning, we design a meta-optimization strategy that enables rapid adaptation to new transaction patterns. The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms the baseline GNN methods. The LLM integration provides an average F1-macro improvement of 8.1% in detecting emerging financial fraud patterns compared to the state-of-the-art BWGNN and F2GNN approaches, validating the effectiveness of combining structural graph learning with LLM techniques.

title: Improving Event-Level Financial Sentiment Analysis with Adaptive Reasoning Order Chain-of-Thought Prompting
abstract: Event-level financial sentiment analysis (EFSA), an emerging research field of considerable interest, aims to extract quintuples of sentiment elements from given financial news articles. Preliminary studies indicate that the sequential reasoning order in chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting considerably impacts the performance of financial information extraction. We propose an adaptive reasoning order CoT framework (ARO-CoT) that enables large language models to determine the optimal query order for the extraction of financial quintuples (company, industry, coarse-grained event, fine-grained event, and sentiment) from Chinese news articles. Specifically, ARO-CoT trains models to automatically select query sequences through reasoning order adaptation, thereby yielding more precise quintuples. To validate the effectiveness of our framework, we conducted comprehensive experiments on the EFSA benchmark. Compared with the previous best EFSA results obtained by retrieval-augmented multipath chain-of-thought prompting, ARO-CoT achieves a new state-of-the-art F1 score and demonstrates robust performance across all EFSA subtasks.

title: Lightweight Orthogonal Adaptive Multi-scale Decomposition for Enhanced Time Series Prediction
abstract: Transformer-based and multilayer-perceptron-based methods have emerged as leading approaches in time series forecasting. While transformer-based architectures demonstrate strength in modeling long-range dependencies, they encounter challenges with computational complexities and overfitting tendencies. In contrast, multilayer-perceptron-based approaches provide computational efficiency and proficiency in temporal dynamics modeling, yet they face difficulties in effectively capturing temporal patterns across complex scales. Real-world time series often exhibit diverse patterns across multiple scales, and future changes are influenced by the complex interactions of these overlapping temporal scales, necessitating high-capacity models. Drawing from the observation of multi-scale entanglement effect in time series, we introduce a lightweight orthogonal adaptive multi-scale decomposition (LOAMD) framework for time series forecasting, building upon the original adaptive multi-scale decomposition approach. Our framework decomposes time series into distinct temporal patterns at multiple scales, leveraging improved multi-scale decomposable mixing to dissect and aggregate these patterns. Additionally, LOAMD introduces lightweight expert design with orthogonal constraints and time–frequency loss functions to achieve superior parameter efficiency while maintaining forecasting accuracy. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our LOAMD framework not only addresses the constraints of existing approaches but also consistently delivers state-of-the-art performance across various datasets.

title: Enhancing the Reliability of Affect Recognition in Social Platforms with Conformal Prediction
abstract: Reliable affect recognition is essential in computational social systems, particularly when analyzing user-generated content on social platforms, where accurate emotion interpretation supports effective content moderation, social analysis, user modeling, and crisis detection. Although large language models (LLMs) achieve strong affect-recognition performance after task-specific fine-tuning, they often remain poorly calibrated, frequently assigning high confidence to incorrect predictions and lacking reliable uncertainty estimates. Such miscalibration undermines the trustworthiness, interpretability, and practical utility of socially intelligent systems. This study applies conformal prediction (CP), including split and adaptive variants, as a model-agnostic post hoc framework that provides finite-sample coverage guarantees and statistically valid uncertainty quantification. We present a unified CP framework that extends existing approaches by developing global, Mondrian, and hybrid conformal predictors for ordinal and multilabel affect recognition, as well as adaptive CP via conformalized quantile regression for regression tasks. Extensive experiments on datasets derived from user-generated social content demonstrate that CP achieves reliable coverage, independent of task type, evaluation metric, or underlying LLM architecture.

title: An Infrastructureless Closed-Loop Authentication Strategy Integrated with Homomorphic Aggregation and Blockchain for the Internet of Vehicles
abstract: As a rapidly developing part of the internet of things, the internet of vehicles (IoV) has extremely high security requirements for data interaction. However, the strong dependence of its existing architecture on roadside units has become a key bottleneck for applications in extreme environments. This study breaks through the traditional infrastructure-dependent model. It proposes a blockchain-based, infrastructureless IoV authentication scheme that combines a homomorphic encryption algorithm and an aggregate signature mechanism to complete vehicle-group identity verification. Key authentication data are uploaded to the blockchain through proof-of-authority consensus to form a tamper-resistant secure ledger. The scheme needs only vehicle cloud assistance to ensure system robustness without roadside units. The proposed framework defends against eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks through homomorphic encryption, defends against impersonation and Sybil attacks through efficient aggregate signatures, and eliminates replay attacks, tampering, and single points of failure by storing immutable authentication records on the blockchain using lightweight proof-of-authority consensus. This ensures secure communication between vehicles. Experimental results show that the scheme achieves good security and performance, providing a new solution for IoV in challenging scenarios.

title: ZX-Diagram T-Count Reduction Based on Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: In fault-tolerant quantum computing systems, the T gates consume more fault-tolerant resources. In this paper, we propose an automated optimization method based on the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. We first translate quantum circuits into ZX-diagrams using ZX-calculus, transforming the circuit optimization problem into a graph rewriting task. Subsequently, the PPO agent, powered by graph neural networks (GNNs) to encode the complex graph structures of the ZX-diagrams, learns to predict efficient transformation paths by focusing on local node and edge features. The PPO algorithm ensures stable policy updates through its clipped objective function, which prevents excessively large and potentially detrimental changes during optimization. Experimental results confirm the method’s effectiveness, showing an average reduction in T-count of 3.12% compared to the baseline approach.

title: Multi-View Fusion: An Advanced Intelligent Computation for Embodied Agents in IoT-Enabled Insulator Inspection Systems
abstract: The intelligent inspection of power grids, a critical component of modern internet of things (IoT) ecosystems, increasingly relies on embodied intelligent agents like drones to ensure operational safety. However, the perceptual accuracy of these agents in identifying insulator anomalies is often hindered by the high cost of acquiring fine-grained, pixel-level annotations for training. To address this issue, this paper proposes an advanced, weakly supervised computation method for the precise localization of insulator anomaly regions, designed for deployment on such embodied agents. Our approach requires only bounding box annotations. Specifically, an object detection network first provides coarse localization of anomalies. Subsequently, a novel multi-view cropping strategy generates diverse visual inputs to enhance local feature representation. These views are then processed by the Segment Anything Model, and a multi-view fusion strategy is employed to considerably improve the accuracy of boundary details. Experiments on a self-built insulator anomaly dataset show that our method achieves localization performance close to fully supervised approaches while substantially reducing annotation costs. This work provides a robust and efficient intelligent computation solution that enhances the perceptual capabilities of embodied agents, demonstrating considerable engineering value for autonomous inspection within smart grid IoT systems.

title: L2L-ESN: A Lead-to-Lead Electrocardiogram Synthesis Network for Assisting Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis
abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring devices, important terminals in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), can provide real-time and rapid myocardial infarction (MI) warning services for large populations. This enables early medical intervention and considerably improves the survival rate of MI patients, thereby alleviating the increasing prevalence of cardiovascular diseases. However, the number of leads in wearable ECG devices is insufficient to accurately diagnose complex cardiac conditions. To address this issue, this study proposes the Lead-to-Lead ECG Synthesis Network (L2L-ESN), which is based on a conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network. It utilizes multihead generation to learn the relationships among leads, synthesize complete 12-lead ECGs from specified leads, and automatically identify the location of MI, thereby maximizing the utilization of available resources and improving diagnostic accuracy under limited-lead constraints, ultimately enabling accurate early warning and timely treatment of MI through wearable devices. The proposed method was evaluated in an IoMT-oriented reduced-lead setting on 2 real-world ECG datasets using waveform similarity metrics, downstream diagnostic tests, qualitative visualization, and deployment profiling. The results demonstrate that L2L-ESN generates more accurate electrocardiographic signals for MI diagnosis, achieving a higher diagnostic accuracy.

title: LM-TTR: Lightweight Monocular Truck-Type Recognition for Source-Based Overload Control
abstract: Truck overloading compromises infrastructure and road safety. Since weight limits vary with axle configurations, accurate truck-type recognition is critical for intelligent source-based overload control systems. However, existing methods usually rely on full-vehicle global views or complex image stitching, which may lead to insufficient recognition accuracy, high deployment cost, or invasive road modification. To address these issues, we propose lightweight monocular truck type recognition (LM-TTR), which infers truck types from visible wheel-hub observations rather than full-vehicle appearance. Specifically, we develop RetinaHub, a lightweight wheel-hub detection network, to locate wheel hubs and recognize their categories from monocular video streams. We then introduce a spatial-prior-constrained neighborhood statistics mechanism to associate and aggregate the detected wheel hubs across frames, thereby deriving stable axle-level structural features, including axle displacement, axle-spacing distribution, and wheel-hub category distribution. Finally, these axle-level features are converted into a standardized code and matched with the standard truck-type library for truck-type recognition. Experimental results show that LM-TTR reduces processing time by more than 92% compared with existing algorithms and can run in real time on an embedded device with 0.5 teraflops computing capability. The proposed method achieves approximately 98% recognition accuracy for common truck types and demonstrates strong robustness under different illumination conditions.

title: BZA-DIA: Blockchain-Based Dynamic Data Integrity Auditing Scheme for Cloud Storage in Artificial-Intelligence-Driven Environments
abstract: Cloud storage is a core pillar of modern data management, particularly in artificial-intelligence-driven applications where the integrity of outsourced data directly affects the reliability of downstream model training and inference. Data integrity auditing serves as a foundational safeguard to ensure that cloud-stored data remain free from tampering. However, prevailing blockchain-based data integrity auditing schemes confront substantial challenges, such as inadequate computational efficiency, breaches in data privacy, and an absence of fairness. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-based, zero-knowledge proof and bilinear accumulator-integrated dynamic integrity auditing (BZA-DIA) scheme. First, the adoption of a bilinear accumulator in place of the conventional Merkle tree structure substantially reduces storage overhead while enhancing the efficiency of dynamic data updates. Second, by harnessing the distributed characteristics of blockchain technology and the privacy-preserving capabilities of zero-knowledge proofs, this scheme effectively mitigates the risk of data privacy breaches. Furthermore, a bidirectional verification mechanism is devised to ensure both fairness and reliability throughout the auditing process. Experimental evaluations reveal that in comparison to the original blockchain-based and zero-knowledge proof-integrated dynamic integrity auditing (BZ-DIA) scheme, BZA-DIA demonstrates considerable enhancements in the efficiency of dynamic operations. Additionally, it surpasses baseline schemes across critical performance indicators, achieving a remarkable reduction in on-chain verification time, validating the scheme as a reliable integrity auditing foundation for cloud storage in artificial-intelligence-driven environments.

title: Obstacle-Aware Distributed Coverage for Multiagent Systems
abstract: Multiagent systems (MASs) are pivotal for large-scale monitoring and exploration, where achieving efficient area coverage is fundamental to comprehensive environmental sensing. However, practical deployments are often hindered by static, nonnavigable obstacles of unknown geometry, which complicate online exploration and degrade coverage efficiency. Existing methods frequently rely on prior environmental knowledge or suffer from redundant exploration near obstacle boundaries. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents a distributed antiflocking coverage algorithm for MASs in unknown environments. Our framework leverages a shared information map mechanism to fuse local observations from neighboring agents, extending situational awareness beyond individual sensing ranges. We introduce an adapted Bug-based navigation strategy to facilitate real-time obstacle detection, boundary following, and incremental mapping. Controlled by a hybrid strategy of antiflocking dynamics and pheromone-guided motion, agents maintain optimal spatial dispersion while minimizing redundant coverage. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively navigates unknown obstacles and considerably reduces overlap in noncoverable regions. The opposite flood-fill mechanism accurately reconstructs obstacle geometries without prior knowledge, while the shared information map mechanism (coverage and pheromone maps) enables each agent to maintain global situational awareness from local observations. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits robust scalability under sensing and communication constraints, validating its suitability for large-scale distributed applications.

title: Ancient Chinese Character Image Restoration: Present Investigations and Future Perspective
abstract: Ancient Chinese character images, including oracle bone inscriptions, bamboo slips, and stele rubbings, are vital carriers of Chinese civilization but are often severely degraded because of aging, resulting in noise, stroke loss, and stylistic distortion. While recent restoration techniques have advanced from traditional pixel-level methods such as skeleton-extraction-based generative adversarial networks to more sophisticated deep generative models such as diffusion models, current approaches remain heavily technology driven. This paper argues that the future of ancient character restoration must evolve beyond purely technical solutions, shifting toward a “human–technology synergy” paradigm that integrates both computational precision and historical authenticity. Embedding historical evolution rules into restoration models, constructing multimodal and cross-era datasets with rich semantic annotations, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computer vision, paleography, and digital humanities are crucial steps toward achieving this goal. By grounding restoration efforts in both technical innovation and humanistic understanding, this paper offers a forward-looking vision for the field, advocating for solutions that are not only accurate in terms of pixel fidelity but also aligned with the historical and cultural context of ancient Chinese characters.

title: Variable-Adaptive Low-Rank Guidance for Diffusion-Based Atmospheric Super-Resolution
abstract: Diffusion-based atmospheric super-resolution can generate realistic high-resolution samples, but unconstrained sampling may still fail to preserve desirable global structure across multiple variables. Such structure is important because downstream meteorological analysis relies not only on local realism but also on coherent large-scale relationships across variables. This study presents a training-free inference-time strategy that augments a pretrained diffusion sampler with adaptive low-rank guidance. The proposed method regulates the effective low-rank correction separately for each atmospheric variable using a signed cosine-based consistency measure computed during sampling. This design allows the low-rank prior to serve as a complementary structural cue rather than a rigid global constraint. To further improve robustness, we introduce a step-level safeguard that disables low-rank guidance when the mean cross-variable consistency measure indicates global incompatibility with the current denoising dynamics. Experiments on HRRR-Mini with near-surface wind components and air temperature as target variables show that the proposed method clearly improves upon both the unguided diffusion baseline and unified low-rank guidance variants in the main stochastic sampling setting. Qualitative comparisons and consistency-trajectory analysis further demonstrate that channel-wise adaptive control better preserves large-scale atmospheric organization while avoiding the over-regularization caused by static low-rank correction. These results suggest that cosine-controlled low-rank guidance provides an effective and interpretable inference-time control mechanism for diffusion-based atmospheric generation.
